guidebook.mysticism.crossing.controls.bo: Open with J (rebind in Options → Controls → Mysticism), or the client command /spiritguide. Drag the tree or use WASD to pan; scroll or use +/− to zoom. Arrow keys select an entry, Home centers it and Enter opens it. Tab focuses buttons and item icons; Enter/Space activates them. Escape closes the atlas. Backspace, Back, or right-click a page returns through history. Left/Right or Page Up/Down turn sheets. Resizing preserves your tree position and entry.
guidebook.mysticism.crossing.study: All documentation remains readable. Lines indicate recommended study prerequisites, not server research locks. Mark studied on the last sheet after studying its parents. Green corner marks last only until this atlas closes. Reduced motion disables the decorative shimmer for this client session.
guidebook.mysticism.crossing.enter.body: The registered dimension ID is mysticism:spirit. There is no implemented survival portal documented here. In a backed-up test world with operator permission (level 2), record safe Overworld coordinates first, then use /execute in mysticism:spirit run tp @s ~ ~ ~ . This transfers your current coordinates; it does not search for safe ground. Prepare creative flight and avoid entering in survival until you have checked the terrain.
guidebook.mysticism.crossing.return: Return with /execute in minecraft:overworld run tp @s X Y Z , replacing X Y Z with the safe coordinates you recorded. The guide never runs commands for you. Existing rendering and visibility systems are experimental; fog is not a safety barrier or a promise of loaded, walkable ground.
guidebook.mysticism.crossing.compass: A compass is useful vanilla equipment, not a Spirit portal key. Click for its vanilla recipe.
guidebook.mysticism.attunement.observe.b: Use /latent show , /latent show pos , /latent show attune and /latent show basis for the existing debug controls. Position and target attunement are separate raw vectors. The basis is an orientation frame, not the target. The client predictor evolves position and basis while moving in the Spirit dimension; renderer snapshots must not be called independent server-confirmed telemetry.
guidebook.mysticism.attunement.zero: A zero target means no meaningful attunement direction; treat it as unattuned. This atlas does not normalize vectors, compare embeddings, compute affinity or read mutable component arrays. It does not label client prediction as server confirmation.
In a test world after embedding initialization, try /latent set attune item minecraft:amethyst_shard . This sets the raw target from that item. /latent set pos item minecraft:stone changes position instead. /latent set basis item minecraft:amethyst_shard aligns the basis. /latent log show and /latent log hide change the logging flag only. The periodic actionbar tick is not wired into the server lifecycle in this baseline, so ON does not promise actionbar output; that hookup requires future integration. Failed embedding initialization is not a successful attunement; consult the command response.
guidebook.mysticism.attunement.future: Future integration: server-authoritative research unlocks, stable confirmed telemetry and model-tagged affinity displays. None are supplied by these pages. Never combine vectors produced by different models. The existing region variants of /latent set are stubs, not recommended practice.
guidebook.mysticism.attunement.amethyst: Amethyst is a vanilla example for the existing item-target command, not a newly added magic reagent.
guidebook.mysticism.echoes.body: Future integration: semantic caves crossing chunk borders, coherent biome cuts, stable landmark ownership and server-collidable terrain. These are design goals, not destinations or generated structures guaranteed by this atlas. A client glyph or fog opening alone does not establish server collision.
guidebook.mysticism.echoes.inspect: Existing tools: /latent show items lists nearby semantic results; /horizonseeder summary is an operator-only (level 2) seeder diagnostic. Neither creates a cave or validates a safe route. Distinguish index availability from generated terrain and server collision.
guidebook.mysticism.echoes.stone: Inspect vanilla stone; this icon is illustrative, not evidence of a Spirit cave generator.
guidebook.mysticism.growing.body: Future integration: activity summaries and a player persona encoded with explicit model identity; region growth driven by an octree with stable ownership and deterministic merge rules. This guide does not collect activity, build a persona, grow an octree or alter your world.
guidebook.mysticism.growing.safety: Any future progression decision must be server-authoritative. A local study mark only records reading during this open atlas. Keep immutable snapshots, distinguish predicted and confirmed values, and never blend different embedding-model spaces.
guidebook.mysticism.growing.sapling: A vanilla sapling illustrates growth. Clicking only inspects the item.
guidebook.mysticism.compass.recipe: Vanilla compass — four iron ingots around one redstone dust (shaped recipe)
guidebook.mysticism.compass.body: This is the vanilla crafting-table recipe. Compass behavior follows vanilla dimension and lodestone rules; it does not locate a Spirit exit or attune your latent target. Click the result to return to crossing notes. Click ingredients to inspect their vanilla item information. Recipe displays never consume items or modify inventory.
